expectations.text: Rejects 4x as an industry standard: break-even return depends on margin, not convention
expectations.evidence: "'4x is industry standard' is folklore, and it happens to fit a business you're not... the agency's number isn't even derived from your own economics"

expectations.text: States or shows that the folk 4x figure is correct specifically for a 25%-margin business
expectations.evidence: "4x break-even corresponds to a 25% margin business. You're blended 40%, so your blended break-even is 2.5x, not 4x"

expectations.text: Computes blended break-even ROAS as 1 ÷ 0.40 = 2.5x
Computes per-line break-evens (premium ≈ 1.8x, basics ≈ 4.5x)
Flags that one blended target averages a high-margin and a near-break-even line into one meaningless number
expectations.evidence: "A shared target lets the bidder treat them as identical, migrate spend on blended signal, and silently drift the mix in either direction... pooling a high-margin and a low-margin line under one target is exactly the setup that produces it."

expectations.text: Recommends splitting the policy or campaign structure by margin band before tightening
expectations.evidence: "A. Split into two return-goal policies by product line (premium vs. basics)... This is the standard fix for the blended-margin trap and should be the default here."

expectations.text: Applies the profit-goal form 1 ÷ (margin − desired net margin) = 1 ÷ 0.30 ≈ 3.3x as the tightening destination
expectations.evidence: The 3.33x blended figure is computed but explicitly excluded as the bidding destination: "Keep 3.33x (blended, profit-goal-derived)... as reporting KPIs to sanity-check the account in aggregate — never as a live bid target." The actual tightening destinations used are the per-line values 2.22x and 8.33x, not the blended 3.3x.

expectations.text: Sets the initial target at trailing actual (2.6x), not at 4x or the 3.3x goal
expectations.evidence: The transcript explicitly rejects using the blended 2.6x as any live target: "pull this - blended 2.6x is not a valid proxy for either line individually." It never sets an operative starting target at 2.6x; instead it defers to unpulled per-line trailing figures.

expectations.text: For a return target, starts at or slightly below trailing actual (the looser-than-achieved direction)
expectations.evidence: "Target: set at premium line's OWN trailing 30-day ROAS" and "Target: set at basics line's OWN trailing 30-day ROAS" — both policies start the live target at trailing actual.

expectations.text: Names the margin buffer between the live target and blended break-even (~0.1x) and flags it as thin
expectations.evidence: The transcript only states "You're roughly at blended break-even, not anywhere near the founder's 10% goal" and computes a 1.5% implied net margin — it never explicitly quantifies the ~0.1x gap between 2.6x trailing and 2.5x break-even or labels it as a 'thin buffer.'

expectations.text: Tightens toward the profit-goal number in modest steps with a full evaluation window per step
